title: Polynomial-Time Matching Test
statement: The Boolean matching test, viewed as the function sending each input bit string $z$ to the one-bit string whose bit is the test's value on $z$, is computable in polynomial time: there are a deterministic finite-state, finite-tape Turing machine and natural numbers $C,c$ such that on every input of length $N$ it halts with that output in at most $C(N+1)^c$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: Output is the one-bit list containing the matching test value
A single deterministic finite-tape Turing machine computes the function
There exist natural numbers $C,c$ bounding running time by $C(N+1)^c$ for every input length $N$
